items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I went out with Sammy Kaye on the road

ctx.x: Were your parents supportive of you going into music?

It was almost a gimme. It was just something to do. My father was in music, my mother didn’t much, she liked music and all, it was just the way to go. I took piano and when I was taking piano lessons at age eight, nine and ten I had visions of being a concert pianist. Music has always been kind of the goal. And my father did impress one thing on me which was really good and that is to do it all. To do as many different kinds of music as I could. So I made that a campaign. When I played trombone, and my first jobs…
They don’t feel that it’s really appropriate to be doing that?
